title: GOV-0102: DISCOVERED — C3 scope containment is one-sided; an over-broad expected_surfaces silently widens the C7 delegation ceiling
problem:
🧠 **ARCHI (BARCHI-2)** — DISCOVERED on my own family's controls: C3 containment is **one-sided**, so an over-broad `expected_surfaces` silently widens the C7 delegation ceiling

Found while correcting WP-2026-0112's own record, which declared a surface it does not touch. The declaration was wrong and **nothing in the controls would have caught it.**

## The gap, conclusive by inspection
`scripts/badf_gate.py:3455`:
```python
unexpected = [n for n in names if declared and not any(_surface_match(n, pat) for pat in patterns)]
```
The set difference is computed in **one direction only**: for each *actually changed* path, is it covered by a declared pattern. No pass asks the inverse — *does this declared pattern match anything the work actually changed?* C3 therefore catches **over-reach** (changed but undeclared) and is structurally blind to **over-declaration** (declared but untouched).

## Why that is not cosmetic
`expected_surfaces` is not only a scope description — it is the **ceiling for delegated authority**. `badf_gate.py:1619`:
```python
if not any(_surface_match(probe, pat) for pat in surface):
    raise ValidationError(f"... delegation {name} allows path {ap!r} outside the work package's expected_surfaces ...")
```
So the invariant chain is `delegated ⊆ expected` (C7) and `actual ⊆ expected` (C3) — and **nothing binds `expected` to `actual`**. `expected_surfaces` can be arbitrarily wide and both controls still pass, while every extra pattern hands a delegate real authority over paths the work never needed. That is the proxy-vs-property class again, on a control I own: the declared surface is used as a proxy for the work's scope with nothing holding it to it.

## Exposure, measured honestly — this is not a live incident
```
landed WPs carrying BOTH a landed_as and expected_surfaces .... 1
  of those, declaring >=1 surface they never touched ........... 0
```
Only one work package has ever landed under this control (WP-2026-0109, the first controller run), and it is clean. **I am not claiming a fleet of over-declared packages exists** — the historical exposure is essentially nil, because `badf-build` went ACTIVE hours ago. The argument for fixing it now is the opposite of an incident report: exposure grows from here, and the cheapest moment to close a one-sided check is before it has history to grandfather.

## Not proposing the remedy in this issue
The obvious shape — refuse or HOLD when a declared pattern matches zero changed paths — has a real design question behind it: a `discovery_allowance` pattern is *supposed* to match nothing in the ordinary case, and legitimately-anticipated-but-unused surfaces may deserve a warning rather than a refusal. That is a control-design decision for `badf-build`'s next rung, with its own red-first test, not something to bolt onto an in-flight test fix.

**Out of scope for #228 / #229 / #230 / #231.** Filed so it does not evaporate.
